questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose London because of personal connections to the city, but also because King's College London is an excellent institution and has a great political science program. It was important to me that the exchange university offered courses that fit my academic profile and King's College did.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. King's College has a very thoruough welcome week and program that offers both academic and social help. They consistently sent emails leading up to arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You could get great assistance, if needed. The King's international office relugarly sent out information emails and encouraged students to get in touch, if they had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Because I know people in London, I didn't find it too difficult. However, it can take a while to secure a place and it is unfortunately very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a fun experience and helps you make friends off campus. But it's also a long process to find housing, there is a lot of competition for places, and they are expensive...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything is too expensive. Without scholarships or a job while on exchange, the student grant does not cover rent in London.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a little complicated. You are responsible for choosing courses at the right level (eg. Masters) and for ensuring that they don't overlap. If you're on a certain agreement, you also have to make sure that you fulfill the criteria of that agreement - I had to take 50% of my courses from certain departments for example.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was apowerpoint guide, but it was not very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly successful. I got two (our of four) of the classes that I really wanted and they offer enough different modules, that there were others that I also liked.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to register for courses on the day that registration opens, so you get the ones you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were very similar to Copenhagen. The classes were smaller and had more reading for each seminar, so there was more material to go thorugh and you were expected to participate more than in Copenhagen. However, I think they are very comparable institutions.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar, but King's required more student participation than Copenhagen. In my experience, it is more often lecture based teaching in Copenhagen and seminar based teaching in the UK.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Religion and Politics in Western Societies
- Foreign Policy Analysis
- Contemporary Religious Movements
- Postcolonial Political Economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Religion and Politics in Western Societies. It was a great course and really highlighted how much religion still influences politics in the 'secular' west.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really - I had planned everything.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was a lot more expensive that I was expecting! London now has the most expensive public transport....

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine. Unfortunately the campus did not have space for everything and London is a very large city, so very often activities would take about an hour to get to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports society. They have social teams and it's a good way to make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the classic tourist sites, the different parks, great shopping, and good train connections to other interesting places in the UK.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Londoners are very used to different cultures and like meeting people from other places.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and try to approach people first.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that so much socialising is centred around drinking here. Important to know that you can go to the pub without drinking alcohol - that's ok!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and genuinely interested people are in each other. And they're funny

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The academic level is high
2. London is huge so be prepared for a long commute in the morning
3. Have fun and make the most of it :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: King's organise a lot of free talks with very interesting people - make the most of that while you're here!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in London, I think. It's such a beautiful, hectic, cultural and fun city and I have felt very lucky to live here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living with housemates. No one lives in their own flats here, so you just have to get used to sharing your kitchen and bathroom with 'random' people. It can be challenging but also fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
